newsitem.title: FRANCE: French public TV boss rejects "stupid" race.
newsitem.headline: French public TV boss rejects "stupid" race.

text.p: Jean-Pierre Cottet, managing director of French public television channel France 2, said his station did not need to run a "stupid race" for audience share with rival private TV channel TF1.
Presenting the public station's summer programmes on Monday, Cottet also said that France 2 needed to maintain its 25 percent market share.
"Being under that would lead us to lose our status as a popular channel," he told a news conference.
France 2's current budget is 4.6 billion francs a year, of which 52 percent comes from advertising receipts.
Cottet said stronger public financing would allow his station to pull out winning programmes.
"With our audience and programming and with more public finance, we could have programme surprises," he said.
Eric Stemlein, programmes director at France 2, said 80 percent of viewers were at home during the summer.

In July 1996, an average of 43.4 million viewers were at home per week, while in August 1996 this figure was 41.2 percent. In March 1997 the weekly average was 49.5 million, compared with 48.8 million in March 1996.

Several live French television shows are not run during July and August as the country has the reputation for being on holiday at that time. But the economic crisis of the last couple of years has curtailed summer holidays for many people.
